data.title: Suspicious payment demand: "new bank details" from Stadtwerke
data.summary: A letter dated 7 September 2026, apparently from Stadtwerke Musterstadt, claims the bank details have changed. It demands €214.00 to a new IBAN by 11 September 2026 and threatens to cut off power. It shows several signs of a scam.
data.explanation: This letter looks like a payment-redirection scam. It says the old bank account is invalid, asks you to transfer an instalment (Abschlag) to a different account held by "Global Energy Payments s.r.o.", threatens a power cut without notice, and tells you not to reply and to call only a special mobile number. Real utilities rarely do this. Do not pay and do not call the number. Check your last genuine bill or the Stadtwerke website for their contact details, and ask them directly whether the letter is real. If you have doubts, you can also report it to the police or the consumer advice centre (Verbraucherzentrale).

warnings: The payee is 'Global Energy Payments s.r.o.', a foreign-style company name, not the Stadtwerke.
The letter threatens a power cut without notice and demands payment within days, which is a pressure tactic.
It tells you not to reply and to call only a special mobile number, and the email domain (kundenservice-mail.example) does not look like an official utility domain.
The letter is impersonal ('Sehr geehrte Kundin, sehr geehrter Kunde') and announces a change of bank details, a known scam pattern.
The letter's deadline of 11 September 2026 has already passed, so no payment is due under it.
